assessment: A number of different stages of pluripotency have been described in the literature. Ávila-González et al., show that human amniotic epithelial cells (hAECs) can be used to support a unique primed pluripotent state in which cells are biased towards an anterior neural identity. The authors explore the unique identity of these lineage-primed pluripotent cells suggesting they could be used for more efficient neural differentiation. The ability of hAECs to support a pre-patterned cell type that continues to express pluripotency markers also implies new roles for the aminion in patterning and supporting early human embryos.
